saints.name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
saints.legacy: Patroness of the Americas and the unborn
saints.summary: Our Lady of Guadalupe is a celebrated apparition of the Virgin Mary that occurred in 1531 in Mexico. She appeared to Juan Diego, a humble indigenous man, and requested the construction of a church in her honor. Her image, miraculously imprinted on Juan Diego's tilma, remains a symbol of faith and cultural identity for millions in Latin America.

saints.name: Finnian
saints.summary: Saint Finnian was a prominent bishop and teacher in early Ireland, known for his role in establishing monastic schools. He founded the famous monastery of Clonard, which became a center of learning and produced many notable Irish saints. His dedication to his flock and commitment to spiritual education greatly influenced the development of Christianity in Ireland.

saints.name: Valery
saints.summary: Saint Valery was a 6th-century monk and abbot known for his piety and miraculous works. He initially studied under a teacher and later joined the monastery of Saint Anthony before moving to Luxeuil to live under Saint Columban. Valery eventually established a monastic community in the wilderness of Leuconaus, where he performed miracles and became renowned for his sanctity before his death in 619.
